summary: Both Task 17 run artifacts record bindings that do not say which role each binding was for. The producing script wrote `roleId: report.roleId`, `report` has no such property, the value was `undefined`, and JSON.stringify dropped the key. This correction sits beside those artifacts and does not alter them.

defect.site: scripts/run-phase4-kickoff.ts, the `bindings` projection in the run record
defect.why: `runtimeBindingReportSchema` (packages/contracts/src/runtime.ts) is strict and declares no `roleId`. A binding report states what runtime session exists; the preflight candidate is what joins that session to a role contract.
defect.foundBy: `npm run typecheck:scripts`, added the same day because scripts/ had never been in the tsconfig project graph. TS2339 at run-phase4-kickoff.ts(228,26).
defect.fixedOn: 2026-09-14, under the ruling above. The script now takes the role from the candidate.

effect.detail: No provider turn, no binding admission, no preflight check and no domain decision read this field. The round ran as recorded; what was lost is the run record's own statement of which role each binding served.
effect.futureRuns: A future Phase 4 live run under the fixed script would record roleId. No such run is authorized.

recovery.method: Join each binding's agentId to the transcript entries in the same file, which carry roleId and agentId as a pair on every turn.
recovery.corroboration: `agentIdFor` in scripts/phase4-kickoff-preflight.ts derives agentId from roleId as `agent_${roleId.replace(/-/g,'_')}`, and every recovered pair matches that derivation.
recovery.limit: This is a join inferred from agentId, not a statement recorded in the binding row. It is exact for these two runs because all six agentIds are distinct and every one appears in the transcript; it is not a general substitute for the field.

notCorrected: Neither run-attempt-1.json nor run-attempt-2.json is edited. Accepted artifacts record what was produced on the day they were produced; corrections are recorded beside them.
